### 2. Important Limitation — Attorney-Client Privilege

Information typed into LegalZoom's website tools and forms is NOT protected by attorney-client privilege. Information shared directly with a network attorney during a scheduled phone consultation IS privileged.
Rule: Keep sensitive business details — pricing strategy, competitive concerns, liability worries — for the attorney phone calls. Use the online forms only for scheduling and basic context.

### 4. How to Prepare for Each Call

Use the 'Add more details' field when booking — give context before the call so the 30 minutes is spent on answers.
Attach the relevant document when scheduling. Keep it under 10 pages to stay in the included tier.
Write your questions down before the call — lead with the most important first.
Take notes during the call and email yourself a summary immediately after. No transcript is provided.
Save all reviewed documents in your dashboard for quick reference.

### 5. Copyright Registrations — Process and Action Items

Why this matters: Copyright protection exists automatically the moment you create a work — you own it without registering. Registration is what lets you sue for statutory damages (up to $150,000 per willful infringement) instead of only actual damages you can prove. It is the difference between an infringement lawsuit being worth pursuing and not.
Key timing fact — registration does NOT block launch: The Copyright Office takes 3–16 months to complete a registration. That is fine. What matters legally is the FILING DATE, not the completion date. File before (or right at) launch, get your filing confirmation, and launch on schedule. The certificate arriving months later does not hold anything up.
The registration process (via LegalZoom):
Place a copyright order in your LegalZoom account and accept the Terms of Service.
Submit a copy of your work (the "deposit materials"). Unpublished works: 1 copy. Published works: 2 copies. Submit by uploading through the portal, emailing attachments, or mailing physical copies.
LegalZoom reviews, prepares, and submits the application electronically to the U.S. Copyright Office.
Copyright Office completes registration in 3–16 months. Your filing date is what counts.
Published vs. unpublished — which applies: Once the Tool and Guide are for sale (at launch), they are "published" and need 2 deposit copies. If you file BEFORE launch, they are "unpublished" and need only 1 copy. Either works — confirm the status with LegalZoom at filing time so the deposit count is right.
Question to ask on a LegalZoom call (source-available software): "For source-available software where the code is intentionally readable, should I deposit the full source code or only a portion? The Copyright Office allows depositing portions (first and last 25 pages, with trade-secret portions redacted). Does depositing the full source affect my ability to enforce the no-redistribution clause in my license?" For GatewayGuard this tension is small — the whole model is that the code is readable — but confirm it before filing.
Critical timing rule — register the FINAL version: Do NOT register the Tool until the build is final and signed. If you register ascii34's source and then ship ascii35, the registered version will not match what you shipped. Register the source of the final signed build. Same for the Guide — lock v9 first.
